teams.heading: Borthwick hands Greg Fisilau first Test start at openside against All Blacks
teams.body: The Exeter back-rower is among five changes from last week's 37-12 win and wears No. 7 for Saturday's third-place play-off, with Ben Earl staying at the base of the scrum. Fisilau's three England appearances, all off the bench, have brought a try against Japan and 19 carries for 85 metres in 81 minutes. Borthwick said the split "could easily be both (seven and eight)", adding that he expects New Zealand to challenge the breakdown hard and that Fisilau has a big job there.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié vows France will go 'all in' against Springboks in Twickenham final
teams.body: Galthié told reporters on Wednesday that France would try everything to beat the side he called the best in the world again, after the 21-19 win over the Springboks in Paris two weeks ago. France reach Sunday's final without starting locks Emmanuel Meafou and Thibaud Flament, and the coach was blunt about the toll: "There's at least one team's worth of players missing, maybe even two." He put the 2025 and 2026 Six Nations titles, and this final, down to work and method rather than luck.

lead.why: Galthié's on-record pre-final stance is the freshest France event not already run, ahead of predictions, a pundit show and a club transfer.

teams.heading: Ireland hold captain's run at Richmond Rugby Club, not at Twickenham
teams.body: Andy Farrell's squad held their final session on Thursday at Richmond Rugby Club's Athletic Ground. It broke from their usual eve-of-match sessions in the stadium itself, because Twickenham is being readied to host six games in three days. Spirits were high: Jamison Gibson-Park soundtracked the walk from the bus on his portable speaker, and Robbie Henshaw arrived already wearing his new head guard. Assistants Simon Easterby and Andrew Goodman launched spiral kicks before Ciaran Ruddock led a brisk warm-up.

lead.why: The freshest new event about the senior side's preparation for Australia, now that the Prendergast story has run.

Ben White, Jack Dempsey and Scott Cummings all started the 15-12 win over Australia the previous weekend but had dropped out of the squad by Japan week. The reshuffled XV still ran in 11 tries, though it conceded seven first-half penalties — indiscipline BBC Scotland's Tom English argued stronger sides would punish.

teams.heading: WRU and regions agree Pathway 2040 principles for Wales talent pathway
teams.body: The Rugby Management Board has spent recent months reviewing every stage of the player development pathway and flagging its friction points. The board brings together performance leads from Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets, the Welsh Rugby Players Association and the union. The long-term strategy covers the men's professional and national teams. It includes a national talent intelligence network to spot players earlier. Advisory groups drawing in Super Rygbi Cymru clubs, academies and education will now test the thinking, while separate talks on the shape of the men's professional game continue.

lead.why: The Japan selection has already run, so the freshest senior-system event about Wales is the union's agreed long-term talent strategy.

teams.heading: Ex-Puma Benjamin Urdapilleta retires from Perpignan to return home to Argentina
teams.body: Benjamin Urdapilleta has ended his Perpignan contract by mutual agreement, telling Usap supporters in a video that he is returning to enjoy life with his family in Argentina. The 40-year-old fly-half, capped 19 times by the Pumas, made one appearance this season, and its two points lifted his Top 14 tally to 2,619, the most of the professional era. A 2018 champion with Castres, he had come out of retirement to help Perpignan survive last season via the play-off at Provence Rugby.

lead.why: It is the only new item, a former Puma's retirement, while the squad, referee and France-defeat stories have already run or are stale.

teams.body: Beale last played for the Wallabies about five years ago, yet he sits among the replacements for the fifth-place final at Twickenham. The selection has a neat symmetry: he played in the 15-6 defeat by Ireland at Eden Park at the 2011 World Cup, the only previous neutral-venue meeting between the sides. He is not the only selection talking point in Kiss's 23. James Ramm is named to debut on the wing, and Teddy Wilson is in line for a first cap off the bench.

teams.body: Steve Tandy has made five changes for Saturday's ninth-place final and handed the captaincy to Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins, with regular skipper Dewi Lake among those rested on a five-three bench. Reuben Morgan-Williams makes his first Test start at scrum-half, James Botham returns at openside and Sam Costelow keeps the No. 10 shirt. Tandy, whose side beat Japan 28-21 in round four, said: "We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan."

teams.heading: Dave Rennie hands Jordie Barrett captaincy in six changes for England rematch
teams.body: Jordie Barrett becomes the third of the brothers to captain New Zealand, after Scott and Beauden, for Saturday's third-place play-off at Twickenham. Asafo Aumua, Anton Segner, Cortez Ratima, Richie Mo’unga, Leicester Fainga’anuku and Rieko Ioane come into the XV beaten 37-12 by England, with Damian McKenzie back at full-back and Cam Roigard and Beauden dropping to the bench. Rennie said his side took full responsibility for that performance. Will Jordan, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i and Anton Lienert-Brown are listed as injured.

teams.heading: Springboks faced no post-match drugs tests during Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series
teams.body: The BBC reports that anti-doping authorities did not take a single post-match sample across the four-Test series against New Zealand in August and September, though such tests are standard at most elite matches. Three of the Tests were in South Africa and the fourth was in Baltimore. The South African Institute for Drug-Free Sport could have demanded samples after games but referred queries to World Rugby, saying the global body had "jurisdiction" over the matches. World Rugby would not confirm the gap, stressing that every player sits in its year-round, no-notice testing pool.

lead.why: The day's only fresh reported event involving the Springboks, corroborated across two outlets, ahead of pundit commentary and an already-run Kolisi story.
